mainTopic: Why the תורה gives separate לאוין for unfair taking, why יציאת מצרים is mentioned with certain מצוות, and the two levels of רבית and whether בית דין can force it to be returned.
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's question of why the תורה lists so many separate לאוין against taking money unfairly. The לאו of לא תגנבו forbids stealing even as a prank or with a plan to pay double. The לאו of weights makes a person guilty as soon as he hides his weights in salt, before he cheats anyone. A ברייתא explains each word of the פסוק about honest measures: מדה, משקל, and משורה. רבא then explains why the תורה mentions יציאת מצרים with רבית, ציצית and weights: the God who knew who was a בכור also sees hidden cheating. רבינא and רב חנינא apply the same idea to שרצים and discuss why that פסוק says 'המעלה'. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and splits its cases into רבית קצוצה, which is forbidden by the תורה, and אבק רבית, which is forbidden by the רבנן. רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן argue about whether בית דין can force a lender to return רבית קצוצה. The גמרא brings three sources for רבי יוחנן, and the source for רבי אלעזר begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The robbery prohibition sits right next to the worker's wages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its previous answer by pointing out that the לאו of לא תגזול is written in the same פסוק as the hired worker.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written in the section about a hired worker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from just before this point. It supports that answer by showing where the פסוק about גזל is located.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא said the לאו of גזל is needed for someone who holds back a worker's pay. Here it proves that reading from the פסוק's setting: the same פסוק that says לא תגזול also talks about a שכיר's wages. Where a לאו is placed tells us what it is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: The topic or section where something is written

phrases.english: And it is written in the section about a hired worker.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:13

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְעִנְיָינָא דְּשָׂכִיר כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes and supports the answer from just before this point about why the לאו of גזל is needed.
steps.raayaObject: That the לאו of גזל teaches about holding back a worker's wages.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The placement of לא תגזול in the same פסוק as the hired worker's wages (ויקרא 19:13).

steps.title: Why does the תורה need the לאו of לא תגנבו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה wrote לא תגנבו, since other לאוין already forbid taking money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need "You shall not steal," which the Merciful One wrote?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question again, now about לא תגנבו. The next step will give the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already have לאוין against גזל, רבית, and אונאה. So a separate לאו against stealing looks extra. The גמרא wants to know what new thing it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
Why do I need it? (asking why something is not extra)

phrases.english: "You shall not steal" that the Merciful One wrote, why do I need it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:11

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תִּגְנֹבוּ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the לאו of גזל to the next לאו, לא תגנבו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new thing the לאו of לא תגנבו teaches that the other לאוין do not.

steps.title: Stealing is forbidden even to annoy or to pay double
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that stealing is forbidden even if you only want to bother the owner, or even if you plan to pay him double.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: You shall not steal, even to annoy him. You shall not steal, even to pay him the double payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows cases that only the לאו of לא תגנבו forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think stealing is only wrong when you want to keep the item and hurt the owner. The ברייתא says no. Even taking it as a prank, or planning to pay back כפל so the owner ends up with more, is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: For that which was taught in a ברייתא
The double payment a thief pays

steps.whatToRemember: לא תגנבו forbids stealing even when no loss is meant: not as a prank, and not even if you plan to pay double.

phrases.aramaic: לְכִדְתַנְיָא: לֹא תִּגְנֹב – עַל מְנָת לְמֵיקַט,
phrases.english: For that which was taught: Do not steal, even in order to annoy him,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תִּגְנֹב – עַל מְנָת לְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל.
phrases.english: do not steal, even in order to pay the double payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לאו is needed to forbid stealing even to annoy someone or with a plan to pay כפל.

steps.title: רב יימר asks why the לאו about weights is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר asks רב אשי why the תורה wrote a separate לאו about weights, since cheating with weights is already stealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said to רב אשי: Why do I need the לאו the Merciful One wrote about weights?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר asks the same "why is it needed" question about the לאו of false weights. רב אשי will answer next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cheating a buyer with light weights is a way of taking his money. That already seems covered by גזל, so a separate לאו about weights looks extra.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא בְּמִשְׁקָלוֹת, לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: The prohibition the Merciful One wrote about weights, why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרַב אָשֵׁי לָאו דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא בְּמִשְׁקָלוֹת לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same "why is it needed" question pattern on a new לאו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the לאו of weights adds beyond the general ban on גזל.

steps.title: It is about hiding weights in salt
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the לאו is about a seller who hides his weights in salt to make them lighter.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is for one who buries his weights in salt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a first answer: the לאו talks about a specific trick with weights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי points to a particular case: putting weights in salt so they become lighter. This answer is about to be challenged.

phrases.english: He said to him: For one who buries his weights in salt.
phrases.notes: The trick makes the weights lighter, so the buyer gets less than he pays for.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְטוֹמֵן מִשְׁקְלוֹתָיו בְּמֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יימר's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לאו is about hiding weights in salt to lighten them.

steps.title: But that is just plain robbery
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר pushes back: hiding weights in salt to cheat is simply גזל, so it still does not need its own לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is full-fledged robbery!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר challenges רב אשי's answer. The salt trick is still just stealing, so the question comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the case to salted weights does not help. In the end, the seller takes the buyer's money unfairly, which is ordinary גזל. So the לאו still seems extra.

phrases.english: That is full-fledged robbery!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ גָּזֵל מְעַלְּיָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's answer that the לאו of weights is about salted weights.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cheating with salted weights is already covered by the ban on גזל, so a separate לאו is still not needed.

steps.title: He is guilty from the moment he hides them
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the לאו makes the seller guilty as soon as he puts the weights in salt, even before he cheats anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: To make him transgress from the moment of the act.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends his answer. The new point of this לאו is when the sin starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under גזל alone, he would only be guilty once he actually took a buyer's money. This לאו makes the act of preparing the false weights already a sin. That is what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: To transgress it, to be guilty of the לאו
From the time of the act itself

steps.whatToRemember: The לאו of false weights makes a person guilty as soon as he prepares the false weights, even before he cheats any buyer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the תורה forbids even preparing cheating tools, not just using them on a buyer.

phrases.english: To transgress it from the moment of the act.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַעֲבוֹר עָלָיו מִשְּׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the focus from what is forbidden to when the sin begins.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Salted weights are just גזל, and he only sins when he cheats a buyer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The לאו of weights makes him guilty already when he hides the weights in salt.

steps.title: The ברייתא on the פסוק: measuring land fairly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק about honest measures and explains that "במדה" means measuring land: do not measure for one person in summer and the other in the rainy season.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "You shall do no wrong in judgment, in measure, in weight, or in volume." "In measure" refers to measuring land: one may not measure for one person in the summer and for the other in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains each word of the פסוק about weights and measures. It starts with the word במדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says במדה is about measuring land. If two people split a field, it must be measured for both under the same conditions. Measuring one share in summer and the other in winter can give one side more land.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"You shall do no wrong in judgment,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:35

phrases.english: in measure, in weight, or in volume."
"In measure": this is measuring land,
that one should not measure for one person in the summer
and for the other in the rainy season.
phrases.notes: The measuring rope can come out a different length in different weather, so one side would get more.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the same פסוק of weights that רב יימר and רב אשי discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "במדה" forbids measuring land for partners under different conditions, like summer and the rainy season.

steps.title: Weights in salt and frothing liquids
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: "במשקל" means not hiding weights in salt, and "ובמשורה" means not making liquid foam up so it looks like more.
steps.simpleTranslation: "In weight": that he should not bury his weights in salt. "And in volume": that he should not make it froth.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes explaining the last two words of the פסוק. Its explanation of במשקל matches רב אשי's answer from before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משקל is about weights, and the ברייתא uses the same salt case רב אשי gave. משורה is about measuring liquids. Making the liquid foam fills the cup with bubbles, so the buyer gets less than he thinks.

keyTerms.meaning: He makes it froth or foam up

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק covers every kind of measuring: land (מדה), weights (משקל), and liquids (משורה). Cheating in any of them is a לאו.

phrases.english: "In weight": that he should not bury his weights in salt.
"And in volume": that he should not make it froth.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמִּשְׁקָל שֶׁלֹּא יַטְמִין מִשְׁקְלוֹתָיו בְּמֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 8, and its salt case matches רב אשי's answer in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "במשקל" forbids hiding weights in salt. "ובמשורה" forbids frothing liquids to make the measure look full.

steps.title: A small measure teaches about all larger measures
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes with a קל וחומר: if the תורה is strict about the tiny משורה, it is surely strict about every larger measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious by a קל וחומר? The משורה is only one thirty-third of a לוג, and still the תורה was strict about it. So the תורה is surely strict about a הין, half a הין, a third of a הין, a quarter of a הין, a לוג, half a לוג, and a quarter of a לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its teaching on honest measures. It argues that if the תורה forbids cheating with a very small measure, it obviously forbids cheating with bigger ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions only the משורה, which is a tiny measure. The ברייתא explains why bigger measures did not need to be listed: if cheating is forbidden even in something this small, it is surely forbidden in the larger measures. This closes the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a smaller case to a bigger one: if the rule holds for the small case, it surely holds for the big one
A very small measure of liquid, one thirty-third of a לוג
A larger liquid measure, equal to twelve לוגין

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה names the tiniest measure on purpose. If cheating there is forbidden, cheating with any bigger measure is forbidden too.

phrases.english: And are these matters not a קל וחומר?
Just as the משורה,
phrases.notes: Here משורה means a tiny measuring amount of liquid, the smallest measure in the list.

phrases.english: which is only one thirty-third of a לוג,
the Torah was strict about it,
all the more so for a הין and a half הין,
and a third of a הין, and a quarter of a הין,
and a לוג, and half a לוג, and a quarter of a לוג.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא דְּבָרִים קַל וְחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק from Steps 8–9 by explaining why only the smallest measure is named.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on cheating with the tiny משורה teaches, by a קל וחומר, that cheating with every larger measure is forbidden.

steps.title: Why does the תורה mention יציאת מצרים by these three מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why the תורה mentions יציאת מצרים next to רבית, ציצית and weights.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why did the תורה mention leaving מצרים next to the law of רבית, next to ציצית, and next to the law of weights?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new topic. He notices that three different מצוות each come with a reminder of יציאת מצרים, and he asks what the reason is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not about what these מצוות require. It asks why each one is tied to the memory of leaving מצרים. רבא is looking for one shared idea that links all three.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest on a loan, which a Jew may not charge another Jew
Fringes worn on the corners of a garment
Literally 'the Merciful One', meaning God or the Torah

phrases.english: רבא said:
Why do I need that the Merciful One wrote
the going out from Egypt with interest,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:38

phrases.english: the going out from Egypt with ציצית,
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:41

phrases.english: and the going out from Egypt with weights?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:36

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It connects to the weights discussion because weights are one of the three מצוות it lists.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah adds a mention of יציאת מצרים to the מצוות of רבית, ציצית and weights.

steps.title: God, who saw who was a firstborn, also sees hidden cheating
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: God, who could tell in מצרים who was truly a בכור, will also punish people who cheat in hidden ways with רבית, weights and ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One said: I am the One who could tell apart, in מצרים, a drop that became a בכור from a drop that did not. I am also the One who will punish someone who pretends his money belongs to a non-Jew and lends it to a Jew with רבית, someone who hides his weights in salt, and someone who hangs fake-blue קלא אילן on his garment and says it is תכלת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. Each mention of מצרים reminds us that God sees what people cannot see, so He sees hidden cheating too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מצרים, only God could know which child was truly a בכור. In each of the three cases, the cheating is hidden: the loan looks like a non-Jew's, the weights look normal, and the dye looks like real תכלת. People may be fooled, but God knows the truth and will punish the cheater.

keyTerms.meaning: To punish, to collect what is owed
A cheap blue dye that looks like תכלת
The special blue dye needed for ציצית

steps.whatToRemember: Mentioning יציאת מצרים is a warning: the God who could tell who was a בכור also sees cheating that no person can catch.
steps.confusionAlert: The cheater here is not breaking a new law. The point is that his trick may fool people, but it does not fool God.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I am the One who distinguished in Egypt
between a drop that became a firstborn
phrases.notes: Only God could know which child was really the firstborn, and only those were struck in מכת בכורות.

phrases.english: and a drop that did not become a firstborn.
I am the One who will in the future punish
one who claims his money belongs to a non-Jew
and lends it to a Jew with interest,
and one who hides his weights in salt,
and one who hangs קלא אילן dye on his garment
and says, "It is תכלת."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אֲנִי הוּא שֶׁהִבְחַנְתִּי בְּמִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mentioning יציאת מצרים recalls that God told apart the בכורות. In the same way, He sees and will punish hidden cheating in רבית, weights and ציצית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a pattern the next steps use again: a mention of יציאת מצרים warns against cheating that only God can see.

steps.title: Why is יציאת מצרים mentioned with שרצים?
steps.stepSummary: In סורא on the פרת, רב חנינא asks רבינא why the תורה mentions יציאת מצרים next to the laws of שרצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא came to סורא on the פרת. רב חנינא of סורא on the פרת asked רבינא: Why did the תורה mention leaving מצרים next to the laws of שרצים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that applies the same question to a fourth place in the תורה. רב חנינא asks why יציאת מצרים appears next to the laws of שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question רבא asked, but about a new מצוה. It sets up an answer that uses רבא's pattern for a case of non-kosher food.

keyTerms.meaning: סורא on the פרת, the Euphrates river
Small creeping creatures that are forbidden to eat

phrases.english: רבינא happened to come to סורא on the Euphrates.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲנִינָא מִסּוּרָא דִּפְרָת לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: רב חנינא of סורא on the Euphrates said to רבינא:
The going out from Egypt that the Merciful One wrote
with the laws of creeping creatures, why do I need it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:45

steps.triggerLanguage: יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי שְׁרָצִים, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as רבא in Step 11, now about שרצים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah mentions יציאת מצרים in the section about שרצים.

steps.title: God sees one who sneaks non-kosher fish innards into kosher ones
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers with the same idea: God, who could tell who was a בכור, will punish someone who secretly mixes non-kosher fish innards into kosher ones and sells them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Holy One said, I am the One who could tell apart a drop that became a בכור from a drop that did not. I will punish someone who mixes the innards of non-kosher fish with the innards of kosher fish and sells them to a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers using רבא's pattern. The mention of מצרים warns someone who sells non-kosher fish innards hidden among kosher ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish innards look alike, so the buyer cannot tell the kosher ones from the non-kosher ones. Just as God could see who was truly a בכור, He sees this hidden mixing and will punish the seller. This applies רבא's idea to the laws of forbidden foods.
steps.whatToRemember: In all these places, mentioning יציאת מצרים carries one message: God sees cheating that people cannot detect, and He will punish it.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I am the One who distinguished
between a drop that became a firstborn
and a drop that did not become a firstborn.
I will in the future punish
one who mixes the innards of non-kosher fish
with the innards of kosher fish
and sells them to a Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, אֲנִי הוּא שֶׁהִבְחַנְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חנינא's question from Step 13 with the same pattern רבא used in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mentioning יציאת מצרים with שרצים warns that God, who told apart the בכורות, will punish someone who secretly sells non-kosher fish innards mixed in with kosher ones.

steps.title: רב חנינא sharpens his question to the word 'המעלה'
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא explains that he was not asking about the mention of יציאת מצרים. He was asking why the תורה says 'המעלה' (who brings up) with שרצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What bothers me is the word 'who brings up'. Why is this place different, that the תורה wrote 'who brings up'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא tells רבינא that the answer missed his real point. His question is about one word, 'המעלה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the places רבא listed (רבית, ציצית, weights), the תורה says 'הוצאתי', 'I brought you out'. With שרצים it says 'המעלה', 'who brings you up'. רב חנינא wants to know why the wording changes here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who brings up', the word the Torah uses with שרצים
It is difficult for me; it bothers me
The Merciful One, meaning God or the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב חנינא is asking the same question again. Step 14 answered why יציאת מצרים is mentioned at all. Now he asks only about the word 'המעלה'.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב חנינא speaking back to רבינא.

phrases.english: For me, it is 'who brings up' that is difficult;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:45

phrases.english: what is different here
that the Merciful One wrote 'who brings up'?
phrases.notes: In the other places the תורה says 'brought you out', not 'brings you up'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אנא המעלה קא קשיא לי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 14 did not address what רב חנינא was really asking
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah uses the word 'המעלה' with שרצים instead of 'הוצאתי'

steps.title: רבינא explains 'who brings up' with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes the school of רבי ישמעאל: God said that taking Israel out of מצרים just so they would not make themselves impure with שרצים would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is for what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught. God said: If I brought Israel up from Egypt only so that they would not make themselves impure with creeping creatures, that would be enough for Me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the word question. He uses a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that keeping away from שרצים is so important that it alone would justify taking ישראל out of מצרים. Keeping this law lifts the people up, so the תורה says 'המעלה', 'who brings up'.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל
Creeping or crawling creatures that are forbidden to eat

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְכִדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: He said to him: It is for what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught.
For the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Had I brought Israel up from Egypt
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, so read it as 'had I brought them up'.

phrases.english: only for this one thing,
that they do not make themselves impure with creeping creatures, it would be enough for Me.

steps.triggerLanguage: לכדתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the word question asked in step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Keeping away from שרצים raises up Israel, so the Torah says 'המעלה'

steps.title: Is avoiding שרצים worth more than רבית, ציצית and weights?
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא challenges: is the reward for avoiding שרצים really greater than for רבית, ציצית and honest weights?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is their reward really greater than that of interest, ציצית and weights?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא pushes back on רבינא's answer. If this law is so special, is it worth more than the other three?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'המעלה' means this law lifts ישראל up more, it sounds like its reward is bigger. But why would avoiding שרצים be worth more than רבית, ציצית and weights? If it is not, the תורה should say 'המעלה' there too.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וּמִי נְפִישׁ אַגְרַיְיהוּ טְפֵי
phrases.english: He said to him: And is their reward greater
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the laws of שרצים.

phrases.english: than interest, ציצית, and weights?

steps.triggerLanguage: ומי נפיש אגרייהו טפי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that avoiding שרצים is what 'brings up' Israel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That would suggest a greater reward than the other מצוות, which seems hard to say. If the reward is not greater, the other מצוות should also say 'המעלה'.

steps.title: Not a bigger reward, but שרצים are especially disgusting
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the reward is not bigger. Still, שרצים are disgusting to eat, so avoiding them is what lifts Israel up.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even though their reward is not greater, they are disgusting to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge. The point is not the size of the reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'brought up' here does not mean getting more reward. It means that staying away from disgusting creatures raises the dignity of the Jewish people, and that fits only שרצים.
steps.whatToRemember: 'המעלה' with שרצים does not mean a bigger reward. It means that avoiding something disgusting raises Israel up.

phrases.english: He said to him: Even though
their reward is not greater,
they are disgusting to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אף על גב דלא נפיש אגרייהו טפי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17 and closes the discussion about the פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'המעלה' means the מצוה has a greater reward
steps.terutzMaskana: 'המעלה' refers to the special disgust of שרצים; avoiding them raises Israel's dignity

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's definition of תרבית: were the earlier cases not רבית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, quotes its definition of תרבית with the wheat example, and asks whether this means all the earlier cases were not רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which is תרבית? One who increases in produce. How so? He bought wheat from him for a gold dinar, etc. Is that to say that all the cases we said until now are not interest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next line about תרבית. Then it asks a question about how that line is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks 'which is תרבית?' as if only this wheat case counts. But the earlier cases in the משנה were also forbidden interest. So the wording seems to suggest they were not רבית, and the גמרא will need to explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: A form of interest; extra gained through a loan or deal

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the earlier cases were forbidden. It is about the משנה's wording, which makes it sound as if only this case is תרבית.

phrases.english: And which is תרבית?
One who increases in produce.
How so? He bought wheat from him
for a gold dinar, etc.
Is that to say that all these
that we said until now
are not interest?

steps.triggerLanguage: אטו כל הני דאמרינן עד השתא לאו רבית הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about the פסוקים and returns to the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Defining תרבית with this case seems to suggest that the earlier forbidden cases are not רבית, which cannot be right.

steps.title: The earlier cases are Torah-level, the later ones are rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, and also רבא, answer that the משנה's earlier cases are רבית from the Torah, and from the wheat case onward they are רבית only from the Rabbis.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Up to this point the cases are forbidden by the תורה. From here on, they are forbidden by the רבנן. רבא said the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 19: the earlier cases really are רבית, but they are a different level from the later ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 asked whether the wheat example means the earlier cases were not רבית at all. The answer is that both are forbidden. The earlier cases are forbidden by the Torah, and the later cases are a rabbinic prohibition. So the משנה is moving from the stricter level to the lighter level.

keyTerms.meaning: Until here, meaning the cases before this point in the משנה
From here on, meaning the cases after this point
Forbidden by the words of the Rabbis

steps.confusionAlert: Rabbinic does not mean allowed. The later cases are still forbidden. They are just a lighter level of prohibition than the Torah-level cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between Torah-level and rabbinic רבית is the base for the rest of this section, including whether judges can force the money to be returned.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
Until here, it is of the Torah;
phrases.notes: 'Until here' means the earlier cases in the משנה, before the wheat example.

phrases.english: from here onward, it is of their words.
phrases.notes: 'Their words' means the words of the Rabbis.

phrases.english: And so said Rava:
Until here, it is of the Torah;
from here onward, it is of their words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אבהו עד כאן של תורה מכאן ואילך של דבריהם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19 about whether the earlier cases were not רבית
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the משנה into two levels of prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wheat definition seemed to say that only it counts as real תרבית, so the earlier cases would not be רבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier cases are Torah-level רבית, and the later cases are rabbinic רבית.

steps.title: Applying the פסוק about the wicked and the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that up to this point, the פסוק 'יכין רשע וילבש צדיק' applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to this point the פסוק applies: 'The wicked one may prepare, and the righteous one will wear it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects a פסוק from איוב to the Torah-level cases of the משנה. It is setting up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is understood as a wicked father who collected רבית and a righteous son who inherits it. The son does not have to give the interest back. This line seems to limit that idea to the Torah-level cases only, which is exactly what the next step questions.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked one prepares (collects the money)
And the righteous one wears it (keeps and uses it)

phrases.english: Until here
"The wicked may prepare, and the righteous shall wear."
phrases.notes: איוב 27:17. It's read as a wicked father who took interest and a righteous son who inherits it and keeps it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עד כאן יכין רשע וילבש צדיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the Torah-level and rabbinic split of Step 20 and adds a rule about heirs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the Torah-level cases, the heir of a lender who took interest keeps it, as the פסוק says.

steps.title: Does the פסוק really stop at the Torah-level cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does the פסוק apply only up to here and not further?
steps.simpleTranslation: Only up to here, and not beyond?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the limit set in Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the heir may keep interest that was forbidden by the Torah, which is the stricter case, he should surely be able to keep interest that was only forbidden by the Rabbis. So it makes no sense to limit the פסוק to the Torah-level cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And no more, and not beyond this

phrases.english: Until here, and no more?
phrases.notes: The point: if the heir keeps even Torah-level interest, surely he keeps the lighter rabbinic interest too.

steps.triggerLanguage: עד כאן ותו לא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the limit stated in Step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק applies only to the Torah-level cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stricter case is included, the lighter case should be included all the more

steps.title: Even the Torah-level cases fit the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords it: even up to here, in the Torah-level cases, the פסוק applies, so the rabbinic cases are certainly included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this: even up to here, the פסוק 'The wicked one may prepare, and the righteous one will wear it' applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording from Step 21 so it no longer sounds like a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' changes everything. Now the statement says the פסוק reaches the stricter Torah-level cases too. That means it obviously covers the rabbinic cases. In all cases, the righteous heir keeps the money.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, a correction of what was said before

steps.whatToRemember: An heir does not have to return interest his father collected. This is true for רבית דאורייתא and certainly for רבית דרבנן.

phrases.english: Rather,
even until here
"The wicked may prepare, and the righteous shall wear"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אפילו עד כאן יכין רשע וילבש צדיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22 by rewording Step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed limited to the Torah-level cases only.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק applies even to the Torah-level cases, and so certainly to the rabbinic ones.

steps.title: Names for the two levels of interest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the two levels: the earlier cases are רבית קצוצה, and the later ones are אבק רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to here the cases are fixed interest. From here on, they are only a 'dust' of interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives names to the two groups of cases from Step 20. It is setting up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבית קצוצה is interest that was clearly agreed on when the loan was made, and that is the Torah-level kind. אבק רבית is something that only has a trace of interest in it, and that is the rabbinic kind. These names will be used right away by רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed interest, agreed on at the time of the loan (Torah-level)
Literally 'dust of interest', a trace of interest (rabbinic level)

phrases.english: Until here, it is fixed interest.
From here onward, it is the dust of interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: עד כאן רבית קצוצה מכאן ואילך אבק רבית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the split of Step 20 and gives each level its name
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah-level cases are called רבית קצוצה, and the rabbinic cases are called אבק רבית.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: judges take back only fixed interest
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that judges can force the lender to give back רבית קצוצה, but not אבק רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Fixed interest can be taken back through judges. A 'dust' of interest cannot be taken back through judges.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר states a practical rule: what a court can do about each level of interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower already paid, can he go to בית דין and get the money back? According to רבי אלעזר, the court will force the lender to return Torah-level fixed interest. For the lighter rabbinic kind, the court will not force it.

keyTerms.meaning: Can be taken back by force of judges (a court)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Fixed interest goes out through judges,
phrases.notes: 'Goes out' means the money is taken back from the lender and returned to the borrower.

phrases.english: the dust of interest does not go out through judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אלעזר רבית קצוצה יוצאה בדיינין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two names from Step 24 to give a practical court rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court forces the lender to return רבית קצוצה but does not force him to return אבק רבית.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: judges do not take back even fixed interest
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says that even רבית קצוצה cannot be taken back through judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even fixed interest cannot be taken back through judges.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with רבי אלעזר and says the court cannot force the return of any interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the court will not force the lender to return אבק רבית. They disagree only about רבית קצוצה. רבי אלעזר says the court forces the lender to return it, and רבי יוחנן says it does not.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying רבית קצוצה is allowed. It is still an איסור דאורייתא. He is only saying a בית דין will not force the lender to pay it back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even fixed interest also
does not go out through judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יוחנן אמר אפילו רבית קצוצה נמי אינה יוצאה בדיינין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר in Step 25 about fixed interest
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court does not force the lender to return even רבית קצוצה.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's source for רבי יוחנן: given over to death, not to repayment
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק brings a פסוק from יחזקאל. It says the person who takes interest 'shall not live.' His punishment is death, not paying the money back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What is רבי יוחנן's reason? The פסוק says: 'He gave with נשך and took תרבית; shall he live? He shall not live. He did all these abominations.' This shows he is given over to death, and not to repayment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the source for רבי יוחנן's view from Step 26, that judges cannot force the lender to return רבית קצוצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks only about the lender's punishment, which is death at the hands of Heaven. It says nothing about giving the money back. רבי יצחק reads that silence as a rule: his 'payment' is his punishment, so בית דין does not force him to return the interest.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest (literally 'a bite'), one of the Torah's words for רבית
Interest (literally 'increase'), the other Torah word for רבית
He is given over to death
Being returned, meaning paying the money back

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan?
For the verse says:
"He gave with neshech and took tarbit,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 18:13

phrases.english: shall he live? He shall not live;
he did all these abominations" —
he is given over to death
and not to repayment.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן? דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 26.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that רבית קצוצה is not taken back through judges.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 18:13: the lender's punishment is death, and repayment is never mentioned.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה's source: given over to fear of Heaven, not to repayment
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה brings a different פסוק, from ויקרא. It ties the sin of interest to 'fearing your God,' and not to paying the money back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: The פסוק says: 'Do not take from him נשך or תרבית, and you shall fear your God.' This shows it is given over to fear of Heaven, and not to repayment.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different source for the same view of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק answers the sin of interest with 'fear your God.' That means it is a matter between the person and Heaven. Since the פסוק does not tell him to give the money back, בית דין cannot force him to.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall fear your God
It is given over to fear (of Heaven)

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
the verse says:
"Do not take from him neshech or tarbit,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:36

phrases.english: and you shall fear your God" —
it is given over to fear
and not to repayment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another source for the same view that רבי יצחק explained in Step 27.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that רבית קצוצה is not taken back through judges.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:36: the sin is tied to fear of Heaven, and repayment is never mentioned.

steps.title: רבא: the פסוק itself compares lenders with interest to murderers
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns it straight from the end of the פסוק in יחזקאל, 'his blood shall be on him.' This compares lenders with interest to murderers, and just as a murderer has nothing to give back, a lender with interest is not forced to give the money back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He learns it from the פסוק itself: 'He shall surely die; his blood shall be on him.' Lenders with interest are compared to murderers. Just as murderers are not subject to repayment, so too lenders with interest are not subject to repayment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third source for רבי יוחנן. This time it comes straight from the words of the פסוק, not from what the פסוק leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק and רב אדא learned from what the פסוקים did not say. רבא points to the actual words 'his blood shall be on him,' which put the lender in the same group as a murderer. From that comparison he moves the rule over: no repayment for the murderer, so no forced repayment for the lender either.

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared (a הקש, linking two things in one פסוק)

phrases.english: Rava said:
He learns it from the verse itself:
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק in יחזקאל that רבי יצחק quoted. Now רבא looks at how that פסוק ends.

phrases.english: "He shall surely die; his blood shall be on him."
Lenders with interest are compared to murderers:

phrases.aramaic: מָה שׁוֹפְכֵי דָּמִים לֹא נִיתְּנוּ לְהִשָּׁבוֹן –
phrases.english: just as murderers are not subject to repayment,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַלְוֵי רִבִּית לֹא נָתְנוּ לְהִשָּׁבוֹן.
phrases.english: so too lenders with interest are not subject to repayment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִגּוּפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third source for רבי יוחנן, using the actual words of the יחזקאל פסוק from Step 27 instead of what it leaves out.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that רבית קצוצה is not taken back through judges.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A הקש from 'his blood shall be on him': lenders with interest are compared to murderers.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins the source for רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks what רבי אלעזר's reason is, and he starts to bring a פסוק. The פסוק itself is quoted at the start of the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What is רבי אלעזר's reason? For the פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the other side of the מחלוקת. This line sets up the source for רבי אלעזר, and the actual פסוק comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said in Step 25 that judges can force a lender to give back רבית קצוצה. Just as the גמרא found sources for רבי יוחנן, it now looks for his source too. The proof is not finished here; we first need to see which פסוק is quoted.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar?
For the verse says:
